about: How a treasury pays its adopted budget each month (src/core2/budgets-treasury.ts): which line public pay draws on, which revenue lines a higher treasury pays as aid, and which spending lines buy work from the town's businesses. Each number is tagged SOURCED (with citation), ESTIMATED (with source and spread) or TUNABLE (with the spread it's checked against).

monthsPerYear.source: Calendar year; each line pays a twelfth of the year's adopted amount each month.

usResidents2024.source: U.S. Census Bureau, Vintage 2024 national population estimate for July 1, 2024 (NST-EST2024-POP). The federal government's residents, so the town's share of federal receipts and lines.

daysPerYear.source: Calendar year (the core's calendar-day wage average, src/core2/modules/residents.ts).

fullTimeHoursPerYear.source: U.S. Office of Personnel Management: 2,087 hours is the federal base, 2,080 (40 hours times 52 weeks) the standard full-time work year (5 U.S.C. 5504).

benefitChangeImpulseScale.source: How hard a change to someone's benefit lands on their mood and stress, per share of the benefit it moved (a 29% cut lands as a mood impulse of -0.29 and a stress impulse of 0.29). Checked against the life-event impulses the drives engine reads (lifeEventMoodScale, lifeEventStressScale).

staffBudgetRoomWeight.source: How much the room left on the line staff pay draws on leans an official's decision to hire, against the trait lean (traitDecisionWeight) and staffHireBase it adds to: an exhausted line subtracts up to this much, room for many years of the post's pay adds up to it.

postLines.about: The budget line a public post's pay draws on, by the post's id prefix (longest prefix wins). Staff serve the official's office; town department heads serve their department; an elected official's salary is general administration (the nearest Census function is 25, central staff services).
postLines.source: Census Bureau, Government Finance and Employment Classification Manual (2006, updated 2022): functions 23 (financial administration), 25 (central staff), 62 (police), 24 (fire), 61 (parks), 44 (highways), 50 (housing and community development).

aid.about: Revenue lines a higher treasury in the game pays to a lower one, and the spending lines it pays them from. The payee's line, a twelfth a month, comes from the payer instead of the outside account.
aid.source: Census Bureau, Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances: 'federal aid' is intergovernmental revenue from the federal government; local 'intergovernmental' is revenue from the state (and other local governments). OMB Historical Table 12.3 (fiscal 2025) puts federal grants to state and local governments in the health, income security, transportation, education and community development functions.

providers.about: Spending lines that buy work from private businesses: the share of the line that is purchases (capital outlay and contracted services), paid to the town's businesses of these kinds for the town's share of the line, by how many people each employs. Where the town has none, that part goes to the outside account, recorded as such.

purchasedShare.source: Census Bureau, 2022 Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances: highway capital outlay over total highway spending, state and local (about $128 billion of $230 billion).
Census Bureau, 2022 Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances: housing and community development capital outlay over the function's spending.
Census Bureau, 2022 Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances: parks and recreation capital outlay over the function's spending.

Census Bureau, 2022 Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances: financial administration, judicial and general control spending other than salaries and capital, taken as contracted professional services.
NCES Digest of Education Statistics 2023, Table 236.10: student transportation and operations and maintenance purchased from contractors, a part of current spending.
Census Bureau, 2022 Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances: health spending other than public hospitals' own payroll, taken as care bought from private providers.
